Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:28: And I heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, also a fitting matter concerning vows - he said that one who vows to perform a commandment, behold, at his utterance one angel is created, but its formation is not completed until the fulfillment of the commandment is complete - for it is known (cf. Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 11) that one who performs one commandment acquires for himself one advocate - and one who vows and does not pay his vow, that angel is found hanging and standing, and it is a distress to him until that act of the commandment is completed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:29: And whoever wishes his prayer to be heard and his request granted should strive to complete his vows, as it is written (Psalms 50:14), "offer to God thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High; and call upon Me in the day of trouble, I will deliver you, and you shall glorify Me" - and so it is written in the Book of Job (22:27), "you shall make your prayer to Him, and He shall hear you, and you shall pay your vows... you shall decree a thing, and it shall be established for you." And these vows are certainly vows to Heaven that it is a commandment to fulfill - and this is its saying "and pay your vows to the Most High" - for concerning permitted matters, which are below, worldly matters, the phrase "your vows to the Most High" would not be accurate. Now, measure for measure - for in prayer he asks in speech that the Holy One, blessed be He, do such-and-such for him - He says to him, you fulfill in deed what you vowed, and I too shall do and fulfill the request of your mouth that depends on speech. And it is already known what they said in the Zohar several times (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 77b), "an arousal below, an arousal above" - that one must always precede with an arousal below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:30: And concerning "vows are a fence for abstinence," it is fitting for a wise person not to vow things that need to be annulled, but rather to vow for one day or half a day - as we find (Makkot 24a) Rabbi Yochanan, who would say, I am in a fast until I come home - and this is (Psalms 15:4), "who swears to his own hurt, and does not change." And even for a fast of [certain] hours, so that he can recite the "Aneinu" prayer, it is like this: he accepts upon himself, while it is still day, a fast until a certain hour of the day, and afterward decides to complete the day in a fast, reciting "Aneinu." And this is a good method for one who is weak, that he accept a fast upon himself and not need to have his vow annulled the next day - and when he completes that day in holiness, he accepts upon himself another day like the previous one, and it is found that all his days are in repentance. But he should not accept to make such-and-such a number of consecutive fasts, for immediately his inclination will stand against him with all its ability to nullify him from his service - and if a person does his matters discreetly and deals with his inclination cunningly, like Jacob's dealing with Esau, he can take away its blessing. And along these lines it is possible that the poet intended in saying in the psalm (Psalms 61:9), "so I will sing praise to Your Name forever, that I may daily perform my vows."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:31: However, so as not to forget to accept his vow for another day, it is good that he seek a companion to encourage him, or make a booklet and write his acceptance there, and keep it with him always, so that he remember his matter. And this way is fitting for every person of action, for just as a merchant makes a book to reckon his expenses, so it is fitting that a penitent make a book to reckon his days, whether he spent them properly or not - and through this he fulfills (Psalms 51:5), "and my sin is ever before me."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:32: Further, of this kind of discourse, one must be careful of excommunications and bans - and concerning the punishment of a ban, they elaborate in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 37): know the power of a ban - come and see from the tribes, who were zealous concerning the licentiousness of the tribe of Benjamin - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, you were zealous concerning the licentiousness but not zealous concerning the idol of Micah - and because they were not zealous concerning the idol of Micah, therefore the children of Benjamin killed among them a first, second, and third time, until they fell before the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD and sought to repent, and the Holy One, blessed be He, was appeased toward them, and they placed a ban that all Israel go with them from great to small, as it is said (Judges 21:5), "for the great oath was" - but did all Israel swear an oath? Rather, this teaches you that the ban is the oath - and the men of Jabesh-Gilead were not with them in the assembly and were liable to death, as it is said, "whoever came not up to the LORD at Mizpah shall surely be put to death" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:33: Further there in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Akiva says, the ban is the oath and the oath is the ban, and whoever breaks the oath is as though he broke the ban, and whoever breaks the ban breaks the oath - and whoever knows a matter and does not tell it, the ban comes upon him and consumes him and his timber and his stones, as it is said (Zechariah 5:4), "and I have sent it forth, says the LORD, and it shall come into the house of the thief, and into the house of him who swears falsely by My Name, and it shall lodge inside his house, and shall consume it, its timber and its stones." Know the power of the ban - come and see from Joshua son of Nun, who placed Jericho under a ban - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:34: Further, one must be careful not to say, "let me be excommunicated if I do not do such-and-such," for even if he fulfills the condition, annulment is needed - and so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Tractate Makkot (11b): Rav Yehudah said in the name of Rav, an excommunication, even conditional, requires release - from where do we know this? From Judah, as it is written (Genesis 43:9), "if I do not bring him to you and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever" - and it is written (Deuteronomy 33:6), "let Reuben live and not die," and then, "and this for Judah" - all those forty years Israel were in the wilderness, Judah's bones were rolled about in the coffin, until Moses stood and sought mercy for him, saying before Him, Master of the universe, who caused Reuben to confess [his sin]? Judah [who confessed first, as a model] - immediately, "hear, O LORD, the voice of Judah" - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:35: Further, one must be careful not to pronounce the Name by its letters, as we read in the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (17b): they brought Rabbi Chanina ben Teradyon [before the Romans]. They said to him, why do you occupy yourself with Torah? He said to them, as the LORD my God commanded me. They immediately decreed that he be burned, his wife killed, and his daughter made to sit in a brothel. Him, to be burned, because he would pronounce the Name by its letters - but how could he do this, when we have learned (Sanhedrin, chapter 10, mishnah 1), and these have no share in the World to Come: one who says the Torah is not from Heaven, and that resurrection of the dead is not from the Torah; Abba Shaul says, also one who pronounces the Name by its letters! [Answer:] he did it in order to learn, as it was taught, "you shall not learn to do" [the practices of the nations] but you may learn to understand and to instruct [others] - so why was he punished? Because he pronounced the Name publicly. His wife, to be killed, because she did not protest against him - from here they said, whoever has the ability to protest and does not protest is punished for it - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:36: And the Tosafot wrote (page 18a, s.v. "hogeh"): "pronounces the Name" - one explanation is that he expounds it through the forty-two-letter Name and does with it whatever he wishes; but most explain that he would pronounce explicitly the letters of the Explicit Name, like the letters of other words - and this is not fitting to do, as we say in Pesachim (50a), "not as I am written am I called - I am written with Yud-Heh and called with Alef-Dalet" - and it appears to Rabbi Yitzchak that one should not even mention the letters Yud-Heh as people are accustomed to do, since Yud-Heh is [part of] the Explicit Name - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:37: "To learn" [it is permitted] to do, as was taught, and so on - and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained. However, the Holy One, blessed be He, is exacting with the righteous to a hairsbreadth, and even for the sake of learning, there is regard for the teacher's honor - and the verse "you shall not learn to do" they established as referring to other matters, such as the planting of cucumbers in Sanhedrin (68a), and the likeness of moon-shapes of Rabban Gamliel (Rosh Hashanah 24a). And the Tosafot wrote, and it appears that his text did not have "rather, why was he punished - was it that he pronounced it publicly?" and therefore he needed to give another reason - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:38: Further, one must be careful not to speak slander against Israel, and so it says in the Yalkut (Melachim, siman 218, page 33, col. 3): why are Israel likened to a nut? As it is said, "I went down to the garden of nuts" (Song of Songs 6:11) - just as this nut is smooth, and whoever is not skilled at climbing it immediately falls - one must guard himself from falling from it - so whoever serves Israel must guard himself from taking what belongs to him from under their hand. Moses said (Numbers 20:10), "hear now, you rebels," and it was said to him (ibid. 20:12), "therefore you shall not bring this congregation." Isaiah said (Isaiah 6:5), "and I dwell among a people of unclean lips" - immediately (6:6), "and in his hand a glowing coal [ritzpah]" - what is "ritzpah"? Rabbi Shimon bar Nachmani said, it crushed [ratzatz] the mouth [peh], for he spoke slander against My children. Elijah said (1 Kings 19:10), "for the children of Israel have forsaken Your covenant" - and what was said to him? (19:16), "and Elisha son of Shafat you shall anoint as prophet in your place."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:39: Rabbi Yochanan derived this from this verse (Isaiah 17:1-2), "the burden of Damascus," and so on, "standing in Damascus and proclaiming the cities of Aroer" - but is Aroer not only in the territory of Moab? Rather, there were three hundred sixty-five houses of idols in Damascus, and they would worship each one on its own day, and they had one day when they would worship them all - that same night, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, Elijah, before you accuse My children, go on your way to Damascus and accuse them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:40: Rabbi Abahu and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish were going up to Caesarea. Rabbi Abahu said to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, why are we going up to their city, which blasphemes and curses? Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish got down from his donkey, took some sand, and put it in his mouth. He said to him, what is this? He said to him, the Holy One, blessed be He, does not desire one who speaks slander against Israel, as it is written (Song of Songs 1:6), "do not look at me, that I am swarthy," and it is written (Proverbs 30:10), "do not slander a servant to his master" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:41: And there in the Yalkut (Melachim, siman 217, page 33, col. 3), before this, on the verse (1 Kings 19:19 - actually 19:9), "what are you doing here, Elijah?" - it was taught in the school of Elijah: he should have said before Him, Master of the universe, behold, Your children are the children of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who did Your will in Your world - but he did not do so, and instead said, "I have been very zealous," and so on. The Holy One, blessed be He, began to speak words of consolation to him, saying, when I descended to give the Torah, Israel did not descend with Me, only the ministering angels, who desired their good, as it is said (1 Kings 19:11), "go out and stand on the mountain," and so on, "and after the earthquake, fire" - He waited for him three hours, and he still stood by his first words and said, "I have been very zealous." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, "and Elisha son of Shafat you shall anoint as prophet in your place" - what you intend, he too can do. He said to Him, forever You are zealous, and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:42: And it is good for a person to train his tongue to teach in defense of Israel, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Yelamdenu concerning Gideon, who said (Judges 6:13), "and where are all His wonders?" - in these words: Rabbi Yehudah bar Shalom said, that night was the night of Passover, that he said to him, "and where are all His wonders?" Where are the wonders God did for our forefathers on this night, and struck all the firstborn of Egypt and brought Israel out from there rejoicing? And since he taught in defense of Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is fitting that I reveal Myself in My glory to him, as it is said (ibid. 6:14), "and the LORD turned to him and said, go in this your strength." The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, you have the strength to teach in defense of Israel - by your merit they shall be redeemed, as it is said, "and save Israel" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:43: And further we read in Sanhedrin: Rabbi Acha said, we find that whoever teaches in defense of Israel, the Holy One, blessed be He, exalts him in the world, as it is written (Isaiah 30:18), "and therefore the LORD shall wait, to be gracious to you, and therefore He shall be exalted, to have mercy on you" - from whom do you learn this? From Achimaatz son of Zadok, as it is said (2 Samuel 18:19), "and Achimaatz son of Zadok said, let me run and bring the king news," and, "and he said, is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" And Achimaatz said, "I saw a great tumult," and, "and the king said, turn aside and stand here, and he turned aside and stood" (18:29-30). Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said, had he been a duke, he would have become a governor; had he been a governor, a commander [for his loyal but incomplete report]. "And behold, the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, let my lord the king receive good tidings," and so on, "and the king said to the Cushite, is it well with the young man, with Absalom?" And the Cushite said, "may the enemies of my lord the king... be as that young man," and so on, "and the king was troubled, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept" (18:31-33, 19:1)] - what is "and the king was troubled"? Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chanina said, this alludes to his blows [i.e., the Cushite was made to suffer for his blunt bad news]. Now is this not an a fortiori argument - if Achimaatz, who said neither good nor bad about the king's son, merited all this honor, one who teaches in defense of the children of the Omnipresent, all the more so - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:44: And so in Vayikra Rabbah (Parashah 10:1), "take Aaron," on the verse (Psalms 45:8), "you love righteousness and hate wickedness" - this verse is explained concerning Abraham, who sought merit for the people of Sodom, as explained there. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, you loved to justify My creatures and not to condemn them - "therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows" - what is "above your fellows"? He said to him, by your life, of the ten generations from Noah to you, I did not speak with any one of them, but with you I speak, as it is said (Genesis 15:1), "after these things."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:45: Further, this verse is explained there concerning Isaiah - the Holy One, blessed be He, said, Isaiah My son, they are troublesome, they are rebellious - if you accept upon yourself to be disgraced and struck by My children, you may go on My mission, and if not, you shall not go on My mission. He said to Him, on this condition: "I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to those who plucked out the hair" (Isaiah 50:6), and I am not worthy to go on a mission to Your children. The Holy One, blessed be He, said, Isaiah, "you love righteousness" - you loved to justify My children - "and hate wickedness" - you hated to condemn them - "therefore God, your God, has anointed you" - what is "above your fellows"? He said to him, by your life, all the other prophets received prophecy, prophet from prophet, "and He drew from the spirit that was upon him," and so on (Numbers 11:25), "and they said, the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha" (2 Kings 2:15) - but you, from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Isaiah 61:1), "the spirit of the LORD God is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me," and so on. By your life, all the prophets [prophesied] simple prophecies, but you, doubled consolations - "awake, awake" (ibid. 51:9), "arouse yourself, arouse yourself" (ibid. 51:17), "I will greatly rejoice" (ibid. 61:10), "I, I am He who comforts you" (ibid. 51:12), "comfort, comfort" (ibid. 40:1) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:46: Further, one must be careful not to engage in idle talk in the synagogue - and so Rabbeinu Yaakov wrote (Orach Chaim, siman 151): synagogues and study halls should not be treated with levity, such as jesting, mockery, and idle talk. And in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 131b): whoever converses in the synagogue, woe to him, for he shows separation; woe to him, for he diminishes faith; woe to him, for he has no portion in the God of Israel, for he shows that there is no God and He is not found there, and he has no portion in Him, and does not fear Him, and conducts himself disgracefully toward the supernal repair above - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:47: And although at first glance, from the wording, it appears that all these severities are stated only concerning the time of prayer - as it says right afterward, that at the time Israel arrange in the synagogue the order of songs and praises and the order of prayer, three camps of supernal angels gather - nevertheless, since the synagogue is a holy place, the dwelling of the Shechinah, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, forbade thinking about calculations there at any time, unless they are calculations for a commandment (Tur, ibid.; cf. Megillah 28b) - certainly one should not converse in ordinary or idle talk, which is forbidden even outside the synagogue, as it is written (Deuteronomy 6:7), "and you shall speak of them" - and not of idle matters - from here, one who converses in ordinary or idle talk transgresses a positive commandment (cf. Yoma 19b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:48: The general rule that emerges is that wherever there is holiness, one must conduct oneself with awe, as it is written (Genesis 28:17), "how awesome is this place; this is none other than the house of God." And in the precepts of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Parashat Beshalach, page 59b), it says that the lower synagogue stands corresponding to the supernal synagogue - and when a person pictures this matter in his mind, he shall fear and be afraid and pray with intent, for the supernal synagogue is called a fire of brightness, and the souls of the righteous enter it only to pray, not to converse about idle matters - and correspondingly the synagogue is called a fire of brightness, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ki Teitzei, page 282a), and therefore they call the synagogue "esh nogah" [fire of brightness].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:49: And it is written in Sefer HaRokeach (Laws of Repentance): one who speaks in the synagogue while his companions praise and sing, I apply to him (Jeremiah 12:14), "concerning all my evil neighbors" - "for the ways of the LORD are right, and the just walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them" (Hosea 14:10) - and one who does not join his companions and disdains praising his Maker encroaches on the Creator's territory - "and I will be to them a small sanctuary" (Ezekiel 11:16) - these are the synagogues, in which levity should not be practiced, as we say in chapter 3 of Megillah (28b-29a) - "God stands in the congregation of God" (Psalms 82:1), and one who speaks acts as though he turns his back to Him - He shall say, why did I come and there was no man, I called and none answered (cf. Isaiah 50:2), I stretched out My hand and none paid heed (Proverbs 1:24) - why should the LORD be angry at your voice and say to you, who has required this of your hand, to trample My courts (cf. Isaiah 1:12)? Rather, bow to Him and turn before Him in awe, with a bowed head, in humility, with the treasures of the heart supplicate before Him, and sing before Him with joy, and come before Him with jubilation - then He shall be near to you and found by you, and you shall unify the Name of Heaven with intent of heart, and pray with intent of heart - and when you say "Blessed are You," if you think of idle matters it is as though you mocked Him, not placing His fear upon your face - rather, think that He stands facing you, "I have set the LORD before me always" (Psalms 16:8), and place His fear upon your face and His love within you, and direct your whole heart, and be modest before Him, and confess your sins and seek Him, and He shall be found by you, and you shall bless Him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:50: And if it is not possible for everyone, at least Torah scholars who fear sin should take this matter to heart, and not begin to speak with each other in the synagogue about their business, even not at the time of prayer, so that they conduct themselves with awe in the synagogue - and if someone who has not conducted himself thus speaks to them, they should answer him briefly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:51: And so was the custom of my teacher, peace be upon him, not to speak within the sukkah on the days of the Sukkot festival except in words of Torah, for the holiness of the commandment of the sukkah is great, and the proof is that the wood of the sukkah has holiness attached to it and is forbidden [to use for other purposes] the whole seven days, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sukkah 9a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:52: And so we find that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Emor, end of page 103) that the Patriarchs come to the sukkah, and said: like Rav Hamnuna Sabba, who, when he entered the sukkah, would rejoice and stand at the entrance of the sukkah from within, and say, let us invite the guests. He would arrange the table and stand on his feet and bless, and say, "in sukkot you shall dwell" - sit, supernal guests, sit, sit, guests of faith, sit. He would raise his hands and rejoice and say, happy is our portion, happy is the portion of Israel, as it is written (Genesis 32:9), "for the LORD's portion is His people" - and he would sit - to this point. And above this, the previous column, he called the sukkah "the shade of faith," and said, whoever sits beneath the shade of faith inherits freedom for himself and his children forever, and is blessed with a supernal blessing, and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:53: Behold, a person within the sukkah is surrounded by an air of holiness, and how many holinesses are in it, as explained - and therefore it is fitting to distance oneself from conversation and jesting, but rather fulfill "and rejoice with trembling" - for the place alluded to by the sukkah is joy and trembling, from which judgments are aroused (Zohar, Parashat Acharei Mot, page 65a), and the days of Sukkot are judgment - and the proof is that on the night of Hoshana Rabbah is the sealing of judgment, and these days must be spent in repentance and trembling, for these days are given in order to extend the time for a person to repent, and the notes of the decrees are not handed over to the messengers until the night of the eighth day, Shemini Atzeret, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 220a), in these words: come and see, when judgment is aroused in the world, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits on the throne of judgment, a person must arouse repentance in judgment, to turn from liability - for on that day the notes are written and all found in wrath are written - whichever person repents before his Master, the notes concerning him are torn up; afterward the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints a time before a person, the Day of Atonement, the day of repentance - if he repents from his sins, he repents, and if not, the King commands that the notes be sealed, woe, for repentance must depart from him; if he merits complete, proper repentance, they hang suspended over him until that final day of Atzeret, which is the eighth day, and if he makes complete repentance before his Master, they are torn up; and if he does not merit it, those notes go out from the King's house and are delivered into hand, and judgment is executed, and the notes never return again to the King's house - then the images depart - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:54: Further, one must be careful not to converse in ordinary talk on the Sabbath, and so it is explained in Midrash Tanchuma (beginning of Parashat Bereshit), on the verse (Isaiah 58:13), "and honor it, not doing your own ways, nor finding your own pleasure, nor speaking your own words," in these words: "nor speaking your own words" - like the mother of Rashbi, who, when she was talking on the Sabbath, he said to her, it is the Sabbath day, and be silent. Rabbi Yochanan said, out of necessity they permitted greeting people on the Sabbath - to this point. And so the Tosafot copied this midrash (s.v. "shelo yehei") in the chapter "Elu Kesharim" (Shabbat 113b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:55: And further they said in the Midrash (cf. Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 23): just as He rested from speaking, so you shall rest from speaking - for by the word of the LORD the heavens were made (Psalms 33:6), and His work was speech, and what is said of Him (Genesis 2:2), "and He rested on the seventh day," is a resting from speech - so too a person, likewise.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:56: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 205b), in these words: when Israel enter the synagogue, it is forbidden to occupy oneself even with the needs of the synagogue, but only with matters of praise, prayer, and Torah as is fitting for them - and whoever occupies himself with other matters, worldly matters, on this day, is a person who profanes the Sabbath, and has no portion among the people of Israel. Two angels are appointed over this on the Sabbath day, and they place their hands on his head and say, woe to so-and-so, who has no portion in the Holy One, blessed be He. And therefore one must occupy himself with prayer and with songs and praises of his Master, and occupy himself with Torah - this day is the day of souls, when that bundle of souls is crowned with the praises of their Master - therefore they praise with the praise of the soul, and this is "the soul of every living thing shall bless Your Name, O LORD our God, and the spirit of all flesh" - and there is no praise except from the side of the soul and the spirit, and this day stands in spirit and soul, it is not [a day] of the body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:57: Now, for this reason we shall understand why our Rabbis, of blessed memory, forbade (Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat, chapter 15, halachah 3) asking for one's needs on the Sabbath - that one prays on the Sabbath only seven blessings - because the day is a day of the soul and not a day of the body, and therefore one does not ask for the needs of the body. And from here the discerning reader shall judge to be strict with himself concerning ordinary talk - for if requesting for one's body is forbidden, all the more so is ordinary talk.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:58: Further, one must be careful not to speak while the prayer leader repeats the Amidah, even words of Torah, but rather direct his intent to answer "amen" to each and every blessing, and his ears should be toward what the prayer leader utters from his mouth, and he should place his eyes below and his heart above, just as in his own silent prayer (Yevamot 105b) - and the reason, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 229a), is that these are two unifications, and in the repetition of the Amidah it is a more excellent unification than the previous one, since he answers "amen" to each blessing, for "amen" totals the numerical value of the two Names "Yakdonki" [YHVH and Adonai combined] - which is not the unification when a person prays silently, for then he mentions the LORD by His appellation Adonai, and although his intent is toward YHVH, nevertheless the two Names are not interwoven as one - but in "amen" there is an allusion to the two Names being unified as one, so it is found to be a more excellent unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:59: And this is the wording of Rashbi, peace be upon him, there, in brief: "greater is one who answers amen than one who blesses" - for [in the silent prayer] it is Adonai [facing] YHVH, and their faces and their wings, corresponding to the Name YHVH in the faces, corresponding to the Name Adonai in the wings, "one cherub from one end and one cherub from the other end" (Exodus 37:8) - but when the prayer leader repeats the prayer and one answers amen, it is in the second joining - "amen" - the two Names are joined in the second joining; at first [it was like] the loops corresponding to one another in the boards, which are the joints of the fingers, but with "amen" "and the Tabernacle shall be one" (Exodus 26:6), in which "the curtains shall be coupled together, one to another" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:60: Behold, it is explicit that the prayer leader's repetition of the prayer is a more excellent unification than the previous one, when he prayed silently - for the cherubim are "one cherub from one end," and so on - and if a person speaks during the prayer leader's repetition, he separates the unification, for there is no other speech there but "amen," which indicates the unification.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:61: And so it is proven from here that when there is a repetition of the eighteen blessings by the prayer leader, one should not alter and say part of the prayer aloud, to say the Kedushah, and part silently - for such a prayer has no place, neither silent nor aloud, and nothing like this is found either in the Talmud or the Zohar.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:62: And so it is also proven in Parashat Vayelech (Zohar, Parashat Vayelech, page 285b), that one must have an attentive ear to answer "amen" to every blessing - it says, on the verse (Isaiah 26:2), "who keeps faith [shomer emunim]" - meaning, guards that blessing which the blesser says, and waits to answer "amen" as needed - his soul ascends and proclaims before Him, "open the gates," and so on. And it says further there, we have learned, whoever hears from the blesser and does not intend "amen" concerning him, of him it is said (1 Samuel 2:30), "and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed" - as it says (Malachi 1:6), "you, O priests, who despise My Name" - and at the time it is needed, what is his punishment? Just as he did not open blessings above, so they do not open for him - and not only that, but when he departs from this world, they proclaim before him and say, shut the gates before so-and-so, let him not enter, do not receive him - woe to him, woe to his soul - to this point. And they elaborate further there on his punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:63: And the wise person, whose eyes are in his head, shall weigh whether occupying himself with Torah at the time of prayer is greater or answering "amen," and without doubt they are not of the same category at the time of prayer, for "a word in its proper time, how good it is." And it appears to me that Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi intended this and said, happy is he whose toil is in Torah and gives satisfaction to his Maker (Berachot 17a) - that his toil in Torah be a satisfaction to his Maker - to exclude one who occupies himself with Torah at a time when the Holy One, blessed be He, has no desire for his Torah, in the aspects mentioned - then certainly there is no satisfaction to the Holy One, blessed be He, in his Torah, and it would be better for him not to occupy himself with Torah [then].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:64: And just as one must be careful throughout the prayer leader's repetition not to speak, so one must be careful on Sabbath eve when the prayer leader repeats "Vayechulu," as it is written in Sefer Chasidim: a certain pious man saw another pious man like himself who had died, with his face yellow. He said to him, why is your face yellow? He said to him, because I would speak during "Vayechulu" at the time the congregation says it, and during the blessing "Magen Avot" while it was being said, and during "Yitgadal" - to this point. So Rabbi Yaakov copied this wording (Tur, Orach Chaim, siman 268).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:65: Further, one must be careful not to speak during the reading of the Torah scroll, and they were strict about this in the Zohar - see there (Parashat Pinchas, page 229a), in these words, in Parashat Vayakhel (page 206a): when the Torah scroll is raised there, then all the people must arrange themselves in fear, in awe, in trembling and quaking, all below, and direct their hearts as though they now stand at Mount Sinai to receive the Torah, and be attentive and incline their ears - and no one, neither the people nor anyone else, has permission to open his mouth in Torah, all the more so in another matter, but rather all in fear, as though he had no mouth - and this has been established, as it is written (Nehemiah 8:5), "and when he opened it, all the people stood," and so on, "and the ears of all the people were toward the book of the Torah" (ibid. 8:3) - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:66: Further, one must be careful, when occupied with Torah or prayer, to utter the words of Torah and prayer properly, and not say them in haste and swallowed - and they said in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, page 227a) that just as the body benefits from bread after the wheat is ground and the fine flour separated from the bran and all the husks, so one must grind the words of Torah with one's teeth until the soul benefits from them - in these words: the thin third husk corresponds to the bran of the wheat, for it clings to the wheat and cannot be separated from it until they grind it in millstones, which correspond to the grinding of the mouth - for a person must grind the words of Torah with them until they become like fine, clean flour, and with a sieve, which is the lip, the refuse, which is the bran of Torah, is separated, until a clean, fine-flour halachah is found - at that time the heart and the brain and all the limbs of the body, in which the soul spreads, take it - in the manner that the body is nourished with worldly things, for "one corresponding to the other, God has made" - the bread of the body and the bread of Torah - this is what is written (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 14:67: Further there (Zohar, Parashat Pinchas, page 236a): from here, whoever utters words of Torah must grind them with his teeth and bring forth complete words, and these words are called "complete" - but others, who are fools, who eat words by gulping and do not grind them with their own grinding and with their teeth - what is written of them? (Numbers 11:33), "the meat was yet between their teeth," and so on, "and the anger of the LORD burned against the people" - for they were of the stock of the one who said, "let me gulp down [some of that red stuff]" (Genesis 25:30) - to this point. And this is also brought in this wording in the same passage (Zohar, Parashat Pinchas, page 246a) - see there.
